articles.titleOriginal: Watch – Cape Town Planning Tribunal agreed with officials almost every time
articles.titleJa: ウォッチ–ケープタウン計画裁判所はほぼ毎回当局と合意しています
articles.summaryJa: 13か月以上にわたり、ケープタウンの市町村計画裁判所は1,328件の土地利用および開発案件について判決を下しました。都市計画担当者の推奨事項からの明確な逸脱として記録されたものはありませんでした。
articles.summaryOriginal: Over thirteen months, Cape Town’s Municipal Planning Tribunal ruled on 1,328 land-use and development cases. Not one was recorded as an explicit departure from city planners’ recommendations. The pattern surfaced in a fight over two data centres proposed near Cape Town International Airport, where objectors warned of a 174-megawatt draw on the grid and 4.4 billion litres of water a year, in communities that already struggle to pay municipal bills. Daily Maverick’s Kevin Bloom’s reporting explains what the numbers show, how the city defends them, why the city says the tribunal occasionally disagrees, and why the tribunal’s required independence - set out in national law - is now in question. Reporting by: Kevin Bloom Filmed by: Joel Seboa Edited by: Anda Tolibadi Produced by: Emilie Gambade Creative input by: Malibongwe Tyilo Sub-edited by: Ian Wolstenholme For Daily Maverick’s full report on this issue, please see the link here and here. *** The meeting minutes of Cape Town’s Municipal Planning Tribunal contain one line that recurs so often it becomes background noise: “The MPT approved the application for the reasons set out in the planner’s report.” It appears after almost every case. Cape Town’s Municipal Planning Tribunal, the MPT, is the body that decides how land in the city gets used: rezonings, subdivisions, developments large and small. It is meant to be an independent check on the city’s own planners. I looked at every ruling the tribunal made over thirteen months,

articles.titleOriginal: Questions remain over when NK mines were planted in DMZ
articles.titleJa: NK鉱山がDMZに植え付けられたときに疑問が残っています
articles.summaryJa: 捜査官は、9月21日のDMZ爆発の共同調査中に、軍事境界線の南側で活発な北朝鮮の対人地雷が発見されたと述べ、国連軍は休戦協定違反が発生したと述べた。韓国軍は、地雷が水洗いされたのではなく埋められたことを示す証拠があると述べたが、いつ埋められたのか、韓国軍を標的にするつもりだったのかはまだ明らかになっていない。
articles.summaryOriginal: Investigators said an active North Korean anti-personnel mine was found south of the Military Demarcation Line during a joint probe into the Sept. 21 DMZ explosions, and the United Nations Command said an Armistice Agreement violation occurred. South Korea’s military said the evidence suggests the mines were buried rather than washed in, but it still has not determined when they were planted or whether they were meant to target South Korean troops. North Korea rejected the findings and called the incident a staged farce. A land mine warning sign is seen in a civilian-controlled area near the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) in Yeoncheon, Gyeonggi Province, Wednesday. South Korea’s military and the United Nations Command said the same day that a violation of the 1953 Korean Armistice Agreement had occurred in connection with the recent land mine explosions in the DMZ. articles.titleOriginal: BTS' RM to feature personal art collection at SFMOMA
articles.titleJa: SFMOMAで個人的なアートコレクションを特集するBTSのRM
articles.summaryJa: BTSリーダーRMは、10月3日にサンフランシスコのSFMOMAで開催される展覧会で、彼の個人的なアートコレクションから約140の作品を展示します。RM x SFMOMA ： Between You and Meは2027年2月7日まで開催され、彼のコレクションとSFMOMAとK - POPアーティストとの最初のコラボレーションの最初の美術館展です。
articles.summaryOriginal: BTS leader RM will feature about 140 works from his personal art collection at SFMOMA in San Francisco in an exhibition opening Oct. 3. RM x SFMOMA: Between You and Me runs through Feb. 7, 2027, and is the first museum exhibition of his collection and SFMOMA’s first collaboration with a K-pop artist. The show includes about 180 works selected by RM and the museum, with many of RM’s pieces shown in the United States for the first time. RM said the project is a long self-introduction shaped by his interest in modern and contemporary Korean art. RM of K-pop boy band BTS / Courtesy of BigHit Music
